title: Beyond the To-Do List
titleZh: TODO List × 拖延症解决：从计划到行动
subtitle: From task tracking to meaningful action
summary: Published primary-source research on anti-procrastination TODO tools plus an implementation-ready Start-First MVP PRD. Product concept and validation plan only; no product or traction is claimed.
summaryZh: 基于 Hacker News / Product Hunt 的已发布竞品调研与 Start-First MVP 产品方案，包含可落地功能规格、状态机、76 项验收、隐私规则和验证计划；尚未声称产品上线。
problem: Conventional to-do lists help people remember tasks, but often fail at the moment of starting difficult or emotionally aversive work.
thesis: A lightweight start-first layer that identifies a task's friction and proposes an editable 2–5 minute first action may deliver more value than another full-featured task manager; this remains an unvalidated hypothesis.
findings: Task capture and categorization are not the same as overcoming initiation resistance.
Design strategies cluster around single-task focus, feasible capacity planning, task breakdown, timeboxing and accountability.
User opinions conflict on reminders, AI prioritization, customization and coercive blocking; intervention intensity should be user-controlled.
Reliability is essential: task loss, duplication or reordering complaints can destroy trust before behavior design helps.
Prioritize measuring the start rate of difficult tasks over counting completed low-effort checkboxes.
risks: Public community comments are a non-representative sample and do not establish product efficacy.
Research does not include hands-on QA, retention cohorts or willingness-to-pay experiments.
AI-generated steps require user editing and error handling; forced reminders may worsen some users' anxiety.
PRD and functional specification describe a proposed product only; no shipped prototype, UX test, or measured behavioral improvement yet.
method: Qualitative desk research (2017–2026 discussions, with emphasis on recent signals): Hacker News threads and Product Hunt product/review pages; A/B/C evidence distinctions, first-person criticism and explicit research limitations. 26 linked original source entries.
